content.comment_body: Thank you for reviewing my question. I'm a beginner and have several queries about writing data to memory cards. When using the Data register block, it's triggered by a signal to store selected parameters on the memory card. My questions are: How long does the trigger need to be maintained for the data to be fully written, or is the duration irrelevant? If the trigger stays ON, does the Data register block just start writing from the moment it's triggered? Also, does [product_name] begin a new record every time the system is switched to RUN? I've read that data is only saved to the memory card when the system stops and then starts again, and only the last complete cycle gets transferred. Is this understanding correct? I appreciate any help.
I hope this information is useful.

Thank you [user_name]! I read your reference more thoroughly this time and found useful answers, but it led to another question from the online help. The manual states you can store up to 32 items (digital or analog), each 8 bits. So, 32 x 8 = 256 bits per trigger. Considering each file holds up to 20,000 lines of 256 bits, that’s about 625kB per file. With an 8GB card, is it possible to store around 12,800 files? And lastly, what is the largest card size that the [product_name] version 8 supports? Thank you again.

From the online help: Data for digital I/O and memory must be logged in groups of eight bits, such as I1 to I8, Q9 to Q16, or M17 to M24. For analog data, you select one value to log, like AI1, AQ2, or AM1. When configuring function blocks, you group by eight-bit digital clusters or single analog values according to the data type. You can log a maximum of 32 items—either analog values or eight-bit digital groups—in each data log. Analog values have a minimum of 16 bits. The maximum microSD card size supported is 32 GB.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are asking for clarification about how the Data register block interacts with microSD memory cards—specifically regarding trigger timing, data logging cycles, and maximum memory card capacity. The conversation shows that new users find the documentation confusing and are searching for straightforward details about data writing behavior and storage limitations. Key points like data log sizes and storage boundaries are recognized, but clearer guidance is needed directly in documentation or user assistance tools.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for simple, direct instructions about trigger duration needed for reliable data writes, clear behaviors during repeated RUN/STOP operations, and precise limits on microSD card compatibility. They hope for accessible guidance to understand these functions reliably.
